**Assistant:** **Nothing is broken.** I ran the health check just now (09:48). It found 0 issues.

**Good news from this morning:**
- Meeting Sync ran on its own at 06:00 and worked. This is the first timed run since the fix, so the fix is proven.
- The backup and the nightly email also show OK.
- The old `flush-error` warning is gone.

**Small items left. None of them blocks your work:**
1. At 12:00, check that the backup's new steps ran. I can do this check later today.
2. One setting points to a folder that does not exist: `codex_memory` → `~/.codex/memories`.
3. One test script stops on the Mac because it uses a Windows-only option: `tests/keystone-reconcile.ps1`.
4. The `game-film-timestamps` skill is not on the Mac.
5. `ZoteroInjestion/SETUP.md` still has old Windows steps.
6. The PowerShell launch fix must be done before 2027-03-01. The health check will warn you.

**One item for you only:** turn on Claude's control of PowerPoint. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation. The five-slides PDF and PNG export needs it.

**What to do now. Pick one:**
- **A. Stop system work and go back to the ship queue.** AP Digest ch1 is due 10/30. I recommend this. The system is healthy, and items 2–5 are only tidying.
- **B. I fix items 2–5 now.** This takes about 20–30 minutes. It does not make anything faster.

Do you want me to fix items 2–5 here, or go with A?

**User:** I want to keep rolling with system work until it's done or at a place where we can objectively say, "Hey you're in a much more efficient state."

**Assistant:** I am measuring how much text loads before you type. Desktop sessions start at about 113k tokens. I am now finding what I can cut.

**Assistant:** I found 7 add-ons from your claude.ai account. I never use most of them. Now I am testing whether I can turn them off on this Mac.

**User:** Tool loaded.

**Assistant:** I am checking the skill helper that runs before each message you type. It takes about 1 second each time. Now I am checking how often its hint helps.

**Assistant:** Two choices are yours. Here are the numbers.

**Assistant:** I am writing the notes and saving the changes now.

**Assistant:** I am writing the notes and saving the changes now.

**Assistant:** Done. Here is what changed. Each part has a number behind it.

**What I measured:**
- **Start size.** This is the text that loads before you type anything.
  - Desktop sessions grew from 71k tokens (10-16) to 113k tokens (today).
  - Most of that growth comes from the desktop app's own tools. I cannot remove those.
- **Hooks.** These are small scripts that run on their own during a session.
  - At session start: 0.26 s.
  - On each tool use: 0.06 s.
  - These are fine.
- **Skill helper.** It ran before every message you typed.
  - It took about 0.5 s each time.
  - In 7 days it showed 474 hints. You (or I) used the hinted skill 6 times. That is 1%.

**What I changed (you said yes to the first two):**
1. **Skill helper is off.** Each message is now about 0.5 s faster, and your text no longer goes to TypeSafe. The code is still in `~/.claude/skill-router/`, so it can come back.
2. **Prompt suggestions are off.** Each reply now makes one fewer model request.
3. **New alarm for start size.** The weekly health check now warns you if sessions start more than 10% bigger than today. The warning shows at the top of your next session. I tested it with a fake value, and it caught it.

**The honest result:** You are faster per message, and you use less of your plan per reply. Start size did **not** shrink. It is now watched, so it cannot grow again without a warning.

**Also proven:** Meeting Sync ran on its own at 06:00 today and worked.

**Not checked:** The skill helper change takes effect when a new session starts.

**Optional, for you (2 minutes):** On claude.ai, open Customize and remove these add-ons:
- browser-use
- firecrawl
- data
- pdf-viewer
- cowork-plugin-management

Code sessions never used them. I cannot remove them from the Mac.

**What you do now:** Nothing. Everything is committed and pushed. The details are in `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/2026-10-24-proof-of-changes.md`.

**User:** Was using TypeSafe as a skill router beneficial to us?

**Assistant:** **Mostly no.** Here are the numbers from 10-17 to 10-24.

**What it cost:**
- It added about 0.5 s to every message. At its slowest, it added almost 1 s.
- It sent the first 500 characters of every message to TypeSafe.
- It failed 24 times. Those failures did no harm, because it was built to fail quietly.

**What it gave:**
- It showed 474 hints, and only 6 were followed. That is about 1%.
- Those 6 were `closeout`, `backup` and `writing-for-agents`. Claude finds these skills well without help, because your words name them ("close out", "run the backup"). The helper probably did not change the result.

**Where it did harm:**
- It often hinted at skills that are not turned on, or that we do not use:
  - `desktop-commander:terminal`: 69 times.
  - `claude-mem-cowork:mem-search`: 25 times. This one competes with your own memory system.
  - `firecrawl-monitor`: 23 times.
- Wrong hints like these can push Claude toward the wrong tool.

**Why the 10-23 test looked good:** That test used 9 prompts we picked and labeled ourselves. Your real messages are different. Most of them do not need a skill at all.

**The one real benefit:** You learned how Jev works, with real data, and you can use that in your TypeSafe work. The helper was a good experiment. It was not a good daily tool.

**Verdict:** Turning it off was right. If you want to try it again later, it needs two fixes:
1. Use a skill list with only the skills that are turned on.
2. Show a hint only when it is very sure.

Even then, I expect a small gain, because Claude already picks skills well on its own.

**User:** All right what's another infrastructure improvement we can make?

**Assistant:** I found the next one. The background memory saver loads about 19k tokens of setup text that it does not need. I am checking which model it uses.

**Assistant:** Tests pass. Now I am running one real memory save to measure it.

**Assistant:** I will also make the health check watch this, so it cannot come back without a warning.

**Assistant:** I found and fixed a hidden cost in your background memory jobs.

**What was wrong:**
- After each session, a background job saves what was learned. It runs about 12 times a day on Opus, your most expensive model.
- Each run loaded about 20k tokens of setup text that it does not need: your instruction files, add-ons and hooks.
- Your other session hooks also ran inside each save. That was extra work that nobody asked for.
- The cause was a bug in the Python toolkit that runs these jobs (claude-agent-sdk 0.2.165). The code said "load no settings", but the toolkit silently ignored it.
- Two other memory jobs had the same bug, `compile.py` and `adjudicate.py`. Their notes said they were protected, but they were not.

**What I did:**
- I sent the setting in a way the toolkit does not drop. I fixed it in all 3 jobs.
- I made the test check for this setting. The memory tests pass: 54 of 54.
- I ran one real save to measure it.

**Did it work?** Yes.
- A save with a tiny test conversation now starts at 852 tokens. Before the fix, a matching test started at 23,500 tokens.
- It still uses Opus, so save quality does not change.
- This cuts about 240k Opus tokens a day from the memory saves alone.

**New alarm:** The weekly health check now warns you if the memory jobs start loading that setup text again.

**Limit:** My test save keeps this alarm quiet until 10-27. A regression before then would not be caught.

**What you do now:** Nothing. All of it is committed and pushed.

There is one more possible saving: run the memory saves on Sonnet instead of Opus. That would use less of your plan. The saved notes could be a little weaker, and I have not measured how much. That is your choice, so tell me if you want it.

**User:** Is Sonnet better than haiku  for this task

**Assistant:** I do not know yet. I have not tested this. Here is what I expect, and how to find out for sure.

**What I expect:**
- **Sonnet** will be close to Opus. The task is to read a conversation and write down the decisions, facts and lessons. Sonnet does this well.
- **Haiku** is the cheapest of the three, so it uses the least of your plan. It has a higher risk of 3 problems:
  - It may miss a decision that is only implied.
  - It may save trivial chat that is not worth keeping.
  - It may answer "nothing to save" when something matters.
- These saves feed your knowledge base. A missed fact is lost for good. A cost you overpay is only money.

**What would prove it:** a small test.
1. Take 5 real sessions from this week.
2. Run the same save step on each session with Opus, Sonnet and Haiku.
3. Count how many of the Opus items each model also finds, and how many junk items it adds.

The test costs very little: about 15 short runs.

**Pick one:**
- **A. Run the test, then switch to the cheapest model that keeps at least 90% of the Opus items.** I recommend this.
- **B. Switch to Sonnet now, with no test.** This is a safe guess, but it is not proven.

Do you want A or B?
